title: Palanpur: The Gateway to North Gujarat’s Hills and Heritage
content:
Palanpur

Tucked at the foothills of the Aravalli Range, Palanpur is a charming town in Banaskantha district, Gujarat, known for its scenic beauty, historical temples, and royal legacy. Surrounded by lush hills, gardens, and architectural marvels, Palanpur offers a perfect mix of nature, spirituality, and heritage - making it one of North Gujarat’s most captivating destinations.

A Glimpse into Palanpur’s History

Palanpur’s history dates back several centuries. Once ruled by the Parmar Rajputs and later by the Jhalas of Jhalawar, it flourished under the rule of the Nawab of Palanpur during the British era. The Nawabi heritage still reflects in the town’s architecture, palaces, and gardens. Today, Palanpur is not only a cultural gem but also a thriving commercial hub in North Gujarat.

Top Places to Visit in Palanpur

1. Balaram Palace Resort

Originally built as the summer retreat of the Nawab of Palanpur, Balaram Palace is a magnificent example of neo-classical architecture set amid the Balaram Ambaji Wildlife Sanctuary. Now converted into a heritage hotel, it offers royal comfort and a glimpse into the grandeur of bygone times.

2. Balaram Ambaji Wildlife Sanctuary

Spread over 500 sq. km, this lush sanctuary is home to leopards, hyenas, sloth bears, and various bird species. With its dense forests and picturesque hills, it’s a must-visit for nature lovers and trekkers. The sanctuary is especially beautiful during the monsoon season.

3. Kirtistambh (Victory Tower)

Located in the heart of Palanpur, the Kirtistambh is one of the town’s most iconic landmarks. Built in honor of the Jain Tirthankaras, this intricately carved marble tower stands as a symbol of peace and victory, showcasing exquisite Jain artistry.

4. Motu Derasar (Jain Temple)

Also known as the Shri Pallaviya Parshwanath Jain Temple, this temple is a spiritual and architectural marvel. The intricate marble carvings, detailed domes, and spiritual aura attract devotees and art enthusiasts from across India.

5. Keertimandir (Nawab’s Tomb)

An elegant structure built in memory of the Nawab of Palanpur, Keertimandir features Indo-Islamic architecture and intricate stonework. It reflects the city’s royal legacy and architectural heritage.

6. Jessore Sloth Bear Sanctuary (Nearby)

Located about 45 km from Palanpur, this sanctuary is known for its population of sloth bears and rich biodiversity. It’s an excellent destination for wildlife lovers and photographers.

7. Ambaji Temple (50 km)

One of Gujarat’s most sacred pilgrimage sites, Ambaji Temple is dedicated to Goddess Amba. The temple’s divine energy and scenic surroundings make it a popular day trip from Palanpur.

8. Mithi Vav (Stepwell)

A beautiful ancient stepwell located near the city, Mithi Vav is an example of Gujarat’s traditional water architecture. The well’s artistic carvings and symmetrical design are reminiscent of the state’s glorious past.

Nearby Attractions

  • Mount Abu (55 km) - Rajasthan’s only hill station, known for its cool climate and Dilwara Temples.
  • Ambaji (50 km) - A major Shakti Peeth dedicated to Goddess Amba.
  • Taranga Hill (85 km) - Famous for its ancient Jain temples and panoramic hill views.

Best Time to Visit

The best time to visit Palanpur is from October to March, when the weather is pleasant and suitable for exploring temples, wildlife sanctuaries, and hill trails.

Local Cuisine

Enjoy the flavors of North Gujarat’s cuisine - from Thepla, Sev Tameta nu Shaak, and Bajra Rotla to local sweets like Mohanthal and Sukhadi.

How to Reach

  • By Air: The nearest airport is Deesa (40 km), while Ahmedabad Airport (160 km) offers better connectivity.
  • By Rail: Palanpur Junction is a major railway station connecting cities like Ahmedabad, Delhi, and Mumbai.
  • By Road: Well-connected via NH-27, Palanpur is accessible from Ahmedabad, Mehsana, and Abu Road.

faqs.question: What is Palanpur famous for?
faqs.answer: Palanpur is famous for its royal history, Balaram Palace, Jain temples, and its scenic location at the foothills of the Aravalli Range.

faqs.question: What is the best time to visit Palanpur?
faqs.answer: The best time to visit is from October to March, when the weather is cool and ideal for sightseeing and nature exploration.

faqs.question: How far is Palanpur from Mount Abu and Ambaji?
faqs.answer: Palanpur is around 55 km from Mount Abu and 50 km from Ambaji, making it an excellent base for short trips.

faqs.question: Are there wildlife attractions near Palanpur?
faqs.answer: Yes, nearby you can explore Balaram Ambaji Wildlife Sanctuary and Jessore Sloth Bear Sanctuary, both rich in flora and fauna.

faqs.question: What are the top attractions in Palanpur?
faqs.answer: The top attractions include Balaram Palace, Motu Derasar, Kirtistambh, Keertimandir, and Balaram Ambaji Wildlife Sanctuary.

faqs.question: Is Palanpur suitable for a weekend getaway?
faqs.answer: Absolutely. Palanpur offers a perfect weekend escape from Ahmedabad or Mehsana, with its royal charm, serene environment, and scenic drives.
